transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Before we dive in, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I came in because... my family and friends keep saying these bank papers prove nothing was taken from me. But I know better. 

For over a year now, I've known that they're hiding my money. They just use things like paying bills, or, you know, fundraisers and planning trips to cover it all up. So I just have to keep confronting them about it. I'm not gonna stop until they finally tell the truth.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?
No, I haven't. I mean, I don't hear voices or... see anything weird like that. I just see what's right in front of me. So, no.

Aside from this situation with your family and finances, do you generally find it hard to trust other people in your life—like coworkers, friends, or strangers—and have you felt that way for a long time, even before this issue with the money started?

No, not really. I mean... I trust regular people fine. Like strangers or whoever, I don't have any problem with them. It's just my family and the ones covering up my money. 

Before all this started, I didn't have any issues trusting anyone. I even trusted my family back then. So, no, it's not like I think everyone in the world is out to get me or something. It's just the people who are actually doing this to me.
Do you have any medical conditions, take any medications, or use alcohol or recreational drugs that started or changed around the time these beliefs about your family began?

No, I don't have any medical conditions or anything like that. I don't take any medications either. And... no, I don't do drugs or drink, so nothing like that started or changed. I'm completely healthy. Like I said, the only thing going on is what they're doing with my money.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusion (persecutory/theft type) focused specifically on family members hiding money, persisting for over one year. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized thought or behavior, no other psychotic symptoms, and functioning outside the delusional theme appears preserved (trusts strangers/coworkers normally). Onset of belief is not temporally linked to any medical condition, medication, or substance use. The circumscribed nature of the delusion, absence of pervasive distrust predating the belief (ruling out paranoid personality disorder), and absence of hallucinations or disorganization (ruling out schizophrenia) support a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder.
